title: Where it grows
subtitle: Tuscany and central Italy
objectives: Explain the climate and soils it needs

steps.title: Tuscany and beyond
steps.body: Sangiovese is the soul of Tuscany: Chianti, Montalcino, Montepulciano, Carmignano and Morellino di Scansano. It also grows in Umbria, Romagna, the Marche and Lazio. Outside Italy, it's planted in Corsica, as Nielluccio, California, Argentina and Australia, but rarely with the same success.

steps.title: Site-sensitive
steps.body: Sangiovese ripens late and needs warmth, but too much heat makes it flat and jammy. It shows best on hillsides at 250 to 600 m, with good sun and cool nights. Galestro, a crumbly marl schist, and alberese, a hard limestone, give its finest wines. It's prone to rot in wet autumns because of its thin skins.

steps.prompt: Match each regional name to its place.
steps.explanation: Sangiovese takes local names in its best zones.

steps.title: Romagna
steps.body: Across the Apennines, Romagna makes Sangiovese di Romagna, now Romagna Sangiovese DOC, often fruitier and softer. Its sub-zones, like Predappio and Modigliana, are making more serious wines. It shows that Sangiovese isn't only Tuscan.

steps.prompt: Which soils give Sangiovese's finest wines in Tuscany?
steps.explanation: Galestro marl and alberese limestone are prized in Chianti Classico.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sangiovese is the soul of Tuscany, also grown across central Italy
It needs warm hillsides and cool nights
Galestro and alberese give its finest wines
